decisions.reason: F3 overstates the scaling identity: F(a,b)=1 for b>=0 and -1 for b<0 has both positive and negative integrals infinite for a^{-2} da db, so its signed integral is undefined. This is confirmed nonfatal because steps 1.2 and 1.3 already restrict their change-of-variables argument to nonnegative Borel functions and extend only to integrable functions; they correctly establish c(a,b)=a and Delta(a,b)=a^{-1}. F3 is repaired to those domains without changing the Example or the calculation.

The rejection correctly observes that the displayed cutoff statement alone does not force support containment, but overlooks the explicitly cited construction. In items/lem-lch-urysohn-cutoff-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set.md, Proof 1.1 chooses K subset V subset closure(V) subset U with compact closure(V), and Proof 2.1 extends h by zero with support in closure(V) subset U. F1 and step 1.1 explicitly invoke that construction, with its open U replaced by W. Thus supp(f_U) subset W subset U is proved; this is a false positive and the sound item is unchanged.

reviews.reason: After restricting F3 to nonnegative Borel or mu-integrable complex functions, its domains match the cited modular definition and right-translation lemma. The left-translation Jacobian a_0^2 cancels the density scaling, while the right-translation Jacobian a_0 leaves factor a_0. Compact finiteness and second-countable regularity establish the Haar hypotheses; AC supplies the declared countable-choice and modular prerequisites. Consequently Delta(a_0,b_0)=a_0^{-1} and Delta(2,0)=1/2. This is the repair author's local verification, not independent review of the repair.

The cutoff supplier's full construction gives support in the chosen open W, and positivity near e makes its compactly supported cutoff have finite positive integral. AC selects one normalized cutoff per neighbourhood. The compact-kernel integral estimate and strong continuity give left convergence, and density with the norm-one bound extends it to all L1. For strict epsilon bounds, strong continuity can be applied with epsilon/2 (and epsilon/6 in the right-hand estimate). The positive isometric involution sends support to U^{-1}, so the same estimate applied to f* gives right convergence. The statement, AC assumptions, owning page and contract remain sound and unchanged.
